title: Telemetry Stitch: Console Usage Map & Route Cost Demo
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked CobaltPay through the Console's usage map and per-route cost dashboards. Discussion covered KV cache effects, batching, dedicated vs hosted, VPC agent pathing, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot and share benchmark plan + pricing. SE to run a rough cost projection based on sample traffic.
action_items: Priya Kapoor - share pilot runbook and benchmark checklist by 2026-04-27
Alex Nguyen - send pricing sheet and reserved capacity options by 2026-04-24
Maya Chen - provide 3 days of representative traffic logs by 2026-04-26
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff (2-week) once logs received
Redwood to produce latency/cost baseline with current model mix
Follow-up technical deep dive (SE-led) if pilot shows >15% cost variance
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-23 14:00 PDT
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions), John Alvarez (CobaltPay CTO), Maya Chen (Infra), Leo Ortiz (Product), Nina Park (SRE)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Console usage map, per-route dashboards, and cost attribution. Discussed pilot and security requirements.

[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'm Alex, AE here at Redwood, Priya is our solutions engineer, Samir in solutions as well. John, Maya, Leo — thanks for being here.

[00:18] John Alvarez: Thanks Alex, yeah excited to see the console. We mainly want to understand per-route costs — we have a ton of internal routes hitting different models and it's hard to map spend to product features.

[00:28] Priya Kapoor: Great, we'll start with the Usage Map in the Console which stitches telemetry across routes and models, and then we'll hop into per-route cost slices, and finally talk about dedicated vs hosted options and any VPC / compliance questions.

[00:45] Leo Ortiz: Quick note, from product we care about cost per feature and latency budgets — payments flows need sub-200ms tail latency.

[01:05] Maya Chen: And from infra perspective we have strict data residency, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration requirements — SOC2 as a must.

[01:28] Priya Kapoor: Totally, we can show how Console ties audit logs and KMS usage. Ok jumping into screen share, take you to the usage map. You'll see nodes representing routes, color-coded by cost delta.

[01:55] Alex Nguyen: One thing to mention: the usage map aggregates both hosted and dedicated routes if you choose to unify them in the same account — you can filter by deployment mode.

[02:18] [screen noise / small crosstalk]

[02:35] Priya Kapoor: Here on the right is a per-route breakdown. We show tokens, model mix, batching efficiency, prefix cache hit rate — note sometimes transcription shows as K V cash in the export but it's KV cache.

[02:58] John Alvarez: Can you explain how batching efficiency is calculated? We have spikes, franken-batches from async requests.

[03:15] Priya Kapoor: Sure — batching efficacy is our observed tokens per GPU pass metric; we show effective throughput and per-token cost after batching and KV cache reuse. There are knobs to set target latency SLOs that will lower batch sizes for latency-sensitive routes.

[03:42] Maya Chen: Are sequence length distributions visible per route? Some of our routes hit long sequences from transcripts.

[03:56] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we surface sequence percentiles and a histogram. If you click into a route you'll see p50/p90/p99 and a sample of typical inputs. That feeds into our kernel selection and quantization recommendations in Optimize.

[04:20] Leo Ortiz: About attribution — how do you handle cases where a single request touches multiple routes (e.g., rerank then summarize)?

[04:33] Priya Kapoor: We have a request-level trace id mapping; the Console can attribute cost by span or by top-level feature. You can choose last-writer attribution or split attribution across spans. We usually recommend split attribution for product economics.

[04:55] Nina Park: How does the billing tie back to our accounting system? We need exportable CSVs with cost centers.

[05:06] Alex Nguyen: We provide per-route daily exports and a mapping layer where you can tag routes with cost-centers. There's also a S3 export or direct webhook ingestion for billing pipelines.

[05:28] John Alvarez: In practice, what's the gap between the console's estimate and actual invoice? +/- what percent?

[05:40] Priya Kapoor: Typically within 3-7% for token-based usage in Hosted. For Dedicated it's more stable because of reserved capacity. The variance comes from batching assumptions and ephemeral cache warmup.

[06:05] Samir Patel: For heavy KV reuse patterns (like chat apps that use a lot of context), cache hit rates can reduce per-token CPU/GPU work by large amounts — we've seen 20-30% unit cost savings in some cases.

[06:28] Maya Chen: Is the KV cache encrypted and how does KMS tie in? We can't have plaintext context leaving our VPC.

[06:39] Priya Kapoor: If you go Private deployment, keys are customer-managed (bring your own KMS/HSM). For Hosted we support envelope encryption backed by our KMS and we can integrate enterprise KMS on dedicated/private.

[06:58] John Alvarez: Ok, security looks doable. Now can you demo a scenario where we reduce cost by switching model variants?

[07:12] Priya Kapoor: Sure — here's a route that was using a 13B model for simple classify hits. On the console we show a suggested lower-latency/low-cost variant with an expected QoQ accuracy delta metric. You can simulate the performance and cost delta in the UI.

[07:42] [15s pause while Priya clicks]

[07:58] Priya Kapoor: See this simulation pane — it projects token cost, expected latency, and a quality delta based on your eval set if you upload one. It flags regressions where quality drops more than threshold.

[08:15] Leo Ortiz: Can we automate rollouts? We want canary for 10% then 50% then full.

[08:25] Priya Kapoor: Absolutely — rollouts are built-in. You can set metric gates (latency, error rate, quality eval score) and an auto-fallback to previous variant.

[08:40] John Alvarez: If we do a dedicated pool, how do burst requests work? We have weekly spikes during payroll runs.

[08:52] Alex Nguyen: Reserved capacity can be configured with burst buckets. You set baseline throughput and a burst policy that consumes spare capacity or routes to hosted fallback if dedicated is saturated.

[09:12] Maya Chen: That's important. Could you show a billing trend where a route spiked and how we would backfill with hosted?

[09:22] Priya Kapoor: Yep — here is a trend line; you can see when the route hits the baseline and the shaded area is burst. The Console annotates when fallback to hosted occurred and provides projected incremental cost.

[09:45] John Alvarez: We mentioned SOC2 earlier — what artifacts do we get for audits?

[09:54] Alex Nguyen: We can share our SOC2 report, encryption whitepaper, and an architecture diagram. For Private deployments we'll also provide network runbooks and access logs. We'll attach those to the proposal.

[10:12] Nina Park: Do you keep request-level logs indefinitely? We need audit trail for 1 year but with masked PII.

[10:23] Priya Kapoor: We support configurable retention. You can redact PII at ingest time and export secure logs to your own S3 with lifecycle rules. For hosted customers we have retention tiers as an add-on.

[10:42] [slight audio flip / schematic noise]

[10:55] Priya Kapoor: Back to cost attribution — here's a route heatmap that cross references model family, instance type, and region. You can pivot on any dimension.

[11:12] Leo Ortiz: Region-level costs — we have EU-only data residency. Can the Console restrict model serving to eu-west?

[11:22] Alex Nguyen: Yes, routing policies can pin routes to region and also set fallback policies to avoid cross-border serving unless explicitly allowed.

[11:38] John Alvarez: Let's talk pilot — what would a two-week pilot look like?

[11:46] Priya Kapoor: Typical pilot: ingest 3-7 days of traffic to seed telemetry, run baseline for 3 days, then enable suggested optimizations for a week and measure delta. We'll provide dashboards, runbooks, and a pre/post report.

[12:05] Maya Chen: We can provide anonymized logs and ask for a staging-only deployment. Any infra work on our side?

[12:15] Priya Kapoor: Minimal — for hosted pilot you just send API keys and a sample of routes; for a private pilot we'd need a VPC peering or agent deployment.

[12:30] Alex Nguyen: Also we'll provide a billing projection spreadsheet — Samir will run a rough projection using your traffic.

[12:40] Samir Patel: I'll need representative QPS and model mix. If you send three days of logs we can produce a conservative and optimistic projection.

[12:55] John Alvarez: Ok we'll send that. Are there known gotchas in the Console visualizations? Sometimes we see mismatched numbers between our infra telemetry and third-party dashboards.

[13:10] Priya Kapoor: Yeah, common mismatches are due to sampling and differing definitions of tokens or when a request is retried. We include a reconciliation guide in the export and a trace-level map to help align.

[13:28] Leo Ortiz: What about latency budgeting for payments — can the console alert if p99 > 200ms?

[13:36] Priya Kapoor: Yes, alerts with webhook/SMS/Slack are supported and you can tie them to routes or service-level objectives.

[13:50] Maya Chen: If we want to enforce SSO and RBAC, what's the setup time?

[13:58] Alex Nguyen: Onboarding SSO/SAML is usually a day to configure and test. RBAC roles are configurable in the Console. For enterprise we do a short security review.

[14:12] [pause while Alex brings up sample deck]

[14:30] Priya Kapoor: Quick demo of Optimize: it will suggest quantization, a model variant, and batching changes. It shows projected cost/latency impact. You can accept suggestions per route or bulk apply.

[14:52] John Alvarez: Any risk of hallucination or quality loss when moving to quantized models?

[15:00] Priya Kapoor: There's always a tradeoff. Optimize provides a quality delta estimate based on evals and flags any regression exceeding user threshold. For safety-critical flows, we recommend canaries and human-in-loop reviews.

[15:20] Nina Park: Do you support private deployment on-prem? We have a few air-gapped data centers.

[15:29] Alex Nguyen: We do offer on-prem packages for regulated workloads. Those include the private control plane, customer-managed keys, and an offline installer.

[15:45] Maya Chen: Good. Any network requirements for on-prem?

[15:52] Priya Kapoor: Minimal outbound for license check, but we can support fully air-gapped with manual key exchange and periodic syncs offline.

[16:08] [slight overlap / someone types in background]

[16:20] Leo Ortiz: Pricing question — how do you price reserved capacity vs usage?

[16:28] Alex Nguyen: Reserved capacity is a commit with a lower unit cost and predictable throughput. Hosted usage is pay-as-you-go and simpler to get started. We can model hybrid approaches.

[16:45] John Alvarez: If we commit to a year of dedicated, do you offer invoicing terms and enterprise support?

[16:52] Alex Nguyen: Yes, enterprise terms, SAML SSO, higher retention, and a premium support SLA are available on annual contracts.

[17:05] Priya Kapoor: Back to the Console — here's an example where we identified a misrouted endpoint causing 18% extra spend; Console flagged the anomaly and recommended a routing rule change.

[17:22] Maya Chen: Nice. Can the console do anomaly detection on tokens per request so we can flag bad clients?

[17:30] Priya Kapoor: Yes, anomaly detection with z-score and custom thresholds; it can create incidents and attach traces for debugging.

[17:46] John Alvarez: About the pilot report — we want both cost and user-facing metric regressions.

[17:54] Samir Patel: We'll include both: cost delta, latency distribution, and a quality evaluation against your provided prompt set.

[18:08] Leo Ortiz: Some small nit — the UI spelled one of our route names wrong in the preview, could be cause by our internal slash characters.

[18:18] Priya Kapoor: Good catch — route normalization can be tuned in mapping rules so that slashes or query params don't create new buckets.

[18:32] Nina Park: If we export logs to our S3, is it encrypted in transit?

[18:40] Alex Nguyen: Yes TLS in transit, and you can enable SSE-KMS on the destination bucket.

[18:52] John Alvarez: Any blockers on our side to start the pilot in two weeks?

[18:59] Maya Chen: We'll need to scrub PII from logs and get legal sign-off for data sharing. Could you send a DTAs or MSA?

[19:10] Alex Nguyen: We'll send standard pilot DPA and an MSA template. We'll also attach SOC2 and the network runbook.

[19:22] Priya Kapoor: For the pilot we'll need 3 days of traffic logs and an API key for staging. Priya types the checklist into the shared doc.

[19:35] [pause while doc link shared]

[19:48] John Alvarez: Great — let's recap next steps.

[19:55] Alex Nguyen: Recap: Samir will run a cost projection once we get logs, Priya will share the pilot runbook and benchmark checklist, I will send pricing and MSA/DPA, and CobaltPay will provide anonymized logs and internal timelines.

[20:15] Leo Ortiz: Timeline — can we kick the pilot starting May 4th?

[20:22] Alex Nguyen: That should be fine, we'll aim to have materials to you this week.

[20:30] John Alvarez: Sounds good. Any final questions?

[20:35] Maya Chen: One last on SSO provisioning — Alex can you share the SAML metadata?

[20:40] Alex Nguyen: Yes, will attach SAML metadata with the follow-up.

[20:48] [murmurs of thanks]

[20:55] Priya Kapoor: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook, pricing, and pilot kickoff scheduling.

[21:05] John Alvarez: Thanks all, appreciate it.
